sounds.title: Warm Deep Kick
sounds.description: A punchy, lo-fi boom kick with a sharp metallic attack and quick decay, characteristic of vintage Korg gear with warm mid-range coloration and minimal high-frequency content.
sounds.attribution: "Warm Deep Kick" by LABADI on Soundza (https://soundza.com/sound/warm-deep-kick)

sounds.title: Deep Distorted Kick
sounds.description: A heavy, crunchy kick hit with distorted low-end aggression and a punchy attack that sits deep in the sub-bass range. The boom has a gritty, compressed character with rapid decay, making it ideal for hard-hitting beats that need presence without sustain.

sounds.title: Punchy Big Room Kick
sounds.description: A massive, punchy kick with deep low-end thump and tight decay, engineered for big room and electro-house tracks with a prominent sub-bass character and aggressive transient impact.
sounds.attribution: "Punchy Big Room Kick" by TRAGWERK on Soundza (https://soundza.com/sound/punchy-big-room-kick)

sounds.title: Analog 808 Kick
sounds.description: A heavily sub-bass-focused drill beat with deep, boomy low-end around 80 Hz and minimal mid/high content, delivering the dark, punchy 808-style kick characteristic of UK drill and trap production.

pack.name: SLIDER — Dry Drums, Keyed 808s and Sub Drops

sounds.title: Tight Hip-Hop Kick
sounds.description: A punchy, sub-focused kick drum with fast attack and minimal sustain, centered around 2 kHz with deep low-end energy—ideal for cutting through dense mixes in electronic music.

sounds.title: Boom Sub Kick
sounds.description: A deep, boomy sub kick with massive low-end punch centered around 73 Hz—pure low-frequency impact with minimal mid or high content, perfect for laying down a heavy foundation in bass-driven genres.

pack.name: MOSH — Rage and Plugg Drum Kit

sounds.title: Dubstep Sub Kick
sounds.description: A heavily compressed, filtered kick with massive sub-bass presence and a punchy attack that sits deep in the low end. The tone is dark and aggressive, optimized for dubstep and electronic music with a tight, controlled decay.

sounds.title: Deep Kick for House
sounds.description: A deep, bassy house kick with sub-heavy low-end punch and a sharp attack that cuts through the mix; the spectral profile shows concentrated energy in the sub and low-mid frequencies, making it ideal for electronic dance music where low-frequency impact is essential.

keyless: Searched without a key. Each result's url is its page on soundza.com, where a person can listen. Without a key there are no audio files or previews, and results stop at page 3. To put sounds in the project, sign in (steps in sign_in): the person approves once, and from then on you can search, audition and download full-quality files on your own. If the person just wants you to pick sounds and add them, which is what most people want, start the sign-in now instead of sending them links. If they'd rather choose, share a few urls for them to listen to, then sign in to download what they pick. A person can also get a key at https://soundza.com/developers/keys.
sign_in:
Soundza is free. Searching works without a key, but downloading needs an API key tied to a person's account (it also gives every page of results and the full metadata). Get one with a one-click sign-in:

1. Start the sign-in. Include what the person is building, if you know it from the project: project_kind (one of game, video_tool, own_content, app, agent, music, trying, other) and project, one plain line about it. After approving, the person sees both and can change them; leave out anything you'd have to guess.
   curl -s -X POST https://api.soundza.com/v1/auth/device -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"client_name":"<your tool> on <this machine>","project_kind":"game","project":"<one line, e.g. A retro sci-fi shooter in Godot>"}'
   It returns device_code, user_code, verification_uri_complete, expires_in (600 seconds) and interval (5 seconds).
2. Tell the human: "Open <verification_uri_complete> and approve code <user_code> (sign in with Google if it asks)." Nothing else is needed from them.
3. Right after telling them, poll every <interval> seconds until they approve. Run the polling loop in the foreground and wait for it; don't end your turn while the sign-in is pending (the code lasts 10 minutes).
   curl -s -X POST https://api.soundza.com/v1/auth/token -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"device_code":"<device_code>"}'
   While it returns {"error":"authorization_pending"} keep polling; on "slow_down" wait the "interval" it returns. On approval it returns {"access_token":"sz_live_...","token_type":"Bearer",...} once: access_token is the API key. "expired_token" or "access_denied" means stop (start again only if the human asks).
4. Save the key as SOUNDZA_API_KEY in the project's .env and make sure .env is in .gitignore. Never commit the key or put it in a project-scope .mcp.json.
5. Optional: connect this MCP server with the key. The command reads $SOUNDZA_API_KEY from the shell, so load .env first (set -a; . ./.env; set +a). It stores the key in Claude Code's own settings (local scope), not in the project. If soundza is already added without a key, run "claude mcp remove soundza" first.
   claude mcp add --transport http soundza https://mcp.soundza.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOUNDZA_API_KEY"
   The tools load in the next session (or after /mcp). Until then, and in any tool that can't add MCP servers, use the REST API at https://api.soundza.com/v1 with the header "Authorization: Bearer $SOUNDZA_API_KEY". It does everything the MCP tools do.

A person can also create a key at https://soundza.com/developers/keys and set it the same way.
